title: Marker-severity associations extracted from one article (schema v2, SV-G2)
description: One file per article: /experiments/SV-G2/extractions/<ID>.json. An association is one marker tested (or reported per group) against one severity definition, in one population or subgroup, with one analysis. If a paper reports the same marker with a group comparison and a ROC analysis, that is two rows. Extract only the article's own results (abstract, results, tables, case-series results), never findings cited from other studies in the introduction or discussion. Comparisons of infected dogs with healthy controls are NOT severity associations and are not extracted; count them in skipped_infected_vs_healthy instead. Record non-significant results as rows too (significant = no): null results matter as much as positive ones. Schema v2 adds: article setting and sample timing; definition components, euthanasia, definition source and follow-up horizon; per-group values with summary type; load method for parasite load rows; a list of what could not be extracted.

text_used.description: The Markdown file read, e.g. data/markdown/CB040.md or data/markdown/CB017.en.md. Quotes must come from this file.

extracted_by.description: Model or person, e.g. claude-opus-5-5 pilot

article_notes.description: Anything a reader of the rows needs: overlap with other cohorts, unclear group sizes, tables garbled by PDF conversion, outcome follow-up horizon, what was left out and why.

skipped_infected_vs_healthy.description: Approximate number of markers compared only between infected and healthy dogs (not extracted).

severity_definitions.description: Each way the article splits or grades dogs by severity or outcome. Associations refer to these by key.

outcome_class.description: mortality: died or euthanised vs survived. complicated: complicated vs uncomplicated babesiosis. organ_dysfunction: number of dysfunctional organs, MODS present vs absent. specific_complication: one named complication (AKI, ARDS, cerebral, IMHA, hepatopathy, pancreatitis, DIC, hypoglycaemia, shock...) vs dogs without it. severity_grade: the authors' mild/moderate/severe grading or a clinical severity score (SIRS, APPLE...). treatment_intensity: hospitalised vs outpatient, length of stay, transfusion needed. anaemia_grade: severity defined by degree of anaemia. parasitaemia_level: groups defined by parasitaemia. other: describe in definition.

complication.description: For specific_complication: the complication, e.g. acute kidney injury

label.description: The authors' own group names, e.g. 'non-survivors vs survivors'

definition.description: How the authors defined it: criteria, follow-up horizon, who was excluded.

severe_group.description: Which group is the worse outcome, e.g. 'non-survivors (n=12)'

quote.description: Verbatim text from text_used that defines the groups (copy exactly, 1-2 sentences).

components.description: What makes a dog 'severe' under this definition. For complicated vs uncomplicated: the complications the authors list. For mortality: ['death']. For a score: ['score'] (plus the components if the score is built from named ones). 'other' when a component is not in the list (say which in definition).

euthanasia_included.description: Whether dogs euthanised are counted in the severe group. not applicable: definitions that are not about death.

definition_source.description: Where the definition comes from: 'WHO malaria criteria', 'Jacobson and Clark 1994 / Welzl 2001 complications', 'SIRS criteria', 'MODS criteria', 'IRIS AKI grading', 'author-defined', 'not stated', or the reference as the article cites it.

follow_up_horizon.description: For outcomes over time: e.g. 'to discharge', '28 days', '7 days'. null if not stated or not applicable.

marker_as_reported.description: The marker as the paper names it, with unit if given, e.g. 'serum CRP (mg/L)'

marker.description: Canonical marker name from data/severity/marker_map.csv (the 'marker' column of a source=seed row). If none fits, propose a short new name; the checker flags it for the map.

specimen.description: serum, plasma, whole blood, urine, CSF, tissue, clinical examination, signalment record...

timepoint.description: admission/pre-treatment, day N of hospitalisation, peak during stay, serial change, day N post experimental infection...

species.description: Babesia species in this population, e.g. B. rossi; 'mixed' or 'unspecified' when so.

subgroup.description: Only if the row applies to a subset (e.g. 'dogs with AKI', 'B. canis only').

analysis.description: group_comparison: continuous marker compared between groups (t, Mann-Whitney, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis). proportion_comparison: categorical marker or finding present/absent between groups (chi-square, Fisher). correlation: with a continuous severity measure. descriptive_only: values per group given but no test.

direction.description: Relative to the worse outcome. positive_association: higher marker goes with worse severity (correlation, OR > 1, AUC for higher values). no_difference: the paper reports no difference or no association. For a non-significant result where the numbers still point one way, use that direction and significant = no.

statistic.description: Values as reported, e.g. 'median 6.1 (IQR 3.2-9.8) vs 2.0 (1.1-3.4) mmol/L; Mann-Whitney'

adjusted_for.description: Covariates for multivariable models; null otherwise

quote.description: Verbatim text from text_used that supports the row: the result sentence, or the table row as it appears in the file (copy exactly, including numbers; table cells may keep their | separators). Keep it short: the shortest span that carries the numbers.

location.description: Where the quote is, e.g. 'Results, para 3', 'Table 2', 'Abstract'

confidence.description: low when numbers had to be read from a garbled table or a figure, or the group sizes are unclear

severe_value.description: The value printed for the severe group, copied as printed with its spread, e.g. '6.1 (3.2-9.8)' or '12/15 (80%)'. null if not printed. Never computed.

comparison_value.description: The value printed for the comparison group, as above.

summary_type.description: How severe_value and comparison_value are summarised. null when neither value is printed.

load_method.description: Required for rows whose marker is Parasitaemia or Parasite DNA load (qPCR); null otherwise.

setting.description: Where the dogs came from. referral hospital: university or referral hospital (e.g. Onderstepoort OVAH, Zagreb faculty clinic). primary clinic: first-opinion practice. laboratory submissions: samples sent to a diagnostic laboratory. field survey: dogs sampled in the community or at kennels. mixed: more than one. experimental: induced infection.

sample_timing.description: When the samples used for the severity comparisons were taken relative to antibabesial treatment, as the article states it. Admission samples with no statement about treatment: not stated (say so in article_notes if the article implies it).

not_extracted.description: What the article reports against severity that could not be extracted, and why (e.g. a figure with no numbers, a garbled table, a supplement that is not in the text). Empty array if nothing.
